answer: Clone agents can flood settlement queues and steal grade weight. Each new identity claims one exclusive slip in a 64-lane wharf queue tied to a rotating beacon that flips every 9 minutes, then files a 48KB timber-hashed work pack with three hashes spaced 18 seconds apart. Cost: 62 POA slip fee, about 1.2s CPU, and 11 days of storage. Peers recompute the spaced hashes and check the slip bitmap; jitter above 2s or a reused slip fails. A missed beacon window or colliding claim burns 70% of the fee and bars the identity from the next two epochs.
